reply_text:
**Don't merge this yet. The content-type lookup is broken for almost every real filename.** I ran the branch's own code against some sample names and didn't change anything.

**Blocker: `extensionOf` reads the wrong part of the name** (`src/extension.js`)
`name.split('.')[1]` takes the text after the *first* dot, and it doesn't lowercase it. The README says the extension is the text after the *last* dot, lowercased. Actual results:

| name | expected | got | content type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Archive.TAR.GZ` | `gz` | `TAR` | octet-stream ✗ |
| `photo.JPG` | `jpg` | `JPG` | octet-stream ✗ |
| `a.b.pdf` | `pdf` | `b` | octet-stream ✗ |
| `README` | `""` | `undefined` | octet-stream |
| `file.` | `""` | `""` | ok |

Only lowercase names with exactly one dot (like `photo.jpg`) get the right type. That's also the only case the test covers, which is why it passes. A fix along these lines would work:
```js
const i = name.lastIndexOf('.');
return i < 0 ? '' : name.slice(i + 1).toLowerCase();
```
The tests should also cover the cases from the README: more than one dot, uppercase, no dot, and a trailing dot.

**Worth fixing: `safeName`**
- It can't climb directories, which is the main goal. Slashes become `_`, so `a/../../x` turns into `a_.._.._x`.
- Inputs like `..`, `...` or `./` come out as an **empty string**. Anything that joins that onto a directory path would write to the directory itself, so it should reject empty names or fall back to a default.
- Stripping leading dots means `.htaccess` is stored as `htaccess`. That's harmless, but the rename may surprise people.

**Minor**
- `TYPES` only has gz, jpg, png and pdf. `jpeg`, `txt` and `json` etc. all fall back to octet-stream. That may be intended, but it's worth confirming.
- The 0.5.0 changelog entry doesn't mention `safeName`.

Everything else, like the version bump and the docs, looks fine. The extension fix is the only thing blocking the merge.
